title: The pawn breakthrough: giving pawns to make a passed pawn
outcomes: Finds the breakthrough sacrifice in a three-against-three pawn skeleton when it exists
Predicts that the same skeleton is level when the other side moves or when the pawns stand one rank further back
Names the three things to check before trying it: who moves, how far the pawns are from queening, where the kings are

steps.text: A **breakthrough** gives up one or two pawns so that a pawn is left with no enemy pawn in front of it. It needs pawns facing pawns; the classic case is three against three on neighbouring files, and the middle pawn moves first. Look for it when your pawns are further advanced and the kings are far away. Watch one, then find it yourself.

steps.caption: White to move. The sacrifice b6 breaks through; one line is shown.

line.say: White offers the b-pawn. Black can take it with the a-pawn or the c-pawn.
A second offer. The pawn on c6 attacks the pawn on b7.
Black takes the pawn on a5 instead.
White takes on b7. The pawn is one step from queening.
Black's king steps to g7; White has a new queen.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is the sacrifice b6.
The engine rates the position as clearly winning for White (depth 24, evidence not proof).

steps.text: The breakthrough is **not a rule**. Here it works because White's pawns are further advanced, the kings are far from the pawns, and White moves first. Change one of these and the same skeleton may be level. Counting who queens first, and where the kings stand, decides. Having the same number of pawns, or more, does not guarantee it.

steps.title: The same skeleton, the other side to move
steps.prompt: In the first position White to move wins. Now it is Black's move, with every piece where it was. Predict the result.

steps.title: The same skeleton, one rank further back
steps.prompt: White to move wins in the first position. Now the whole skeleton is one rank lower on the board: White's pawns are on the 4th rank, Black's on the 6th. Predict the result.
Before each answer: which did you check first, who is to move, how far each side's pawns are from queening, or where the kings stand? Which one did you forget?
